newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul state bank, KEPCO to issue bonds in London.
newsitem.headline: Seoul state bank, KEPCO to issue bonds in London.

text.p: The Korea Development Bank and electricity-monopoly Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) plan to issue sterling-denominated bonds in Britain, a finance and economy ministry official said on Thursday. A KEPCO official said the company would issue 150 million sterling straight bonds this month. KEPCO plans a roadshow in London next week. He said he estimated the bonds would carry an annual interest rate of 0.70-0.75 basis point over 10-year British Treasury Bond, at around 8.25 percent.
The ministry official said the state-bank planned to issue sterling-denominated bonds equivalent to $320 million.
The ministry official said the issue of sterling-denominated straight bonds would be the first for South Korea in Britain.
"The commission fee is cheaper in Britain at 0.35 percent compared with 0.65 percent in the U.S.," he said.

The KEPCO official said the company had decided to develop a new market as foreign investors tended to shy away from Korean investment facilities following the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel.
"We also want to secure a foothold in Britain ahead of united European countries," he said.
